title: Airbus A380-800

sources.title: FlyByWire A380X documentation: Thrust and Thrust Reverser Control Levers
Airbus A380 flight deck (public descriptions, FlyByWire A380X docs)

intro: The Airbus A380 is the world's largest passenger airliner, with four engines and two pilots. Like smaller Airbus planes it is flown with a side-stick on each outer side. Eight screens show flying data, maps and systems, and the pedestal screens work with a keyboard and trackball. The panels are laid out in the style of the A320 family.

areas.name: Glareshield
areas.text: The strip below the windscreen with the warning lights, screen settings and the autopilot panel.

panels.name: Glareshield: FCU and EFIS control panels
panels.text: The strip under the windscreen holds the warning lights, the screen settings (EFIS) and the autopilot panel (FCU), laid out like the smaller Airbus planes.
panels.context: The pilots use this strip to tell the autopilot what to do and to adjust their map screens.

controls.name: MASTER WARN / MASTER CAUT lights
controls.text: These big lights get the pilots' attention. Red means warning, amber means caution. Pressing a light silences the alarm and resets the light.
controls.context: After pressing it, the pilots read the message on the engine and warning display.

controls.name: EFIS control panels
controls.text: These panels set the pilot's screens: the air-pressure setting for the altimeter, the type and range of the map, and options on the flight and map displays.
controls.context: There is one for each pilot, at the left and right ends of the glareshield.

controls.name: SPD/MACH, HDG/TRK, ALT and V/S knobs

positions.name: PUSH
positions.text: Managed: the flight computer chooses.

positions.name: PULL
positions.text: Selected: the dialled number is used.

controls.text: These knobs set the autopilot targets: speed, heading or track, altitude and climb rate. Pushing a knob lets the flight computer manage the value. Pulling it uses the number the pilot dialled.
controls.context: The pilot dials the instruction from air traffic control here and the autopilot follows it.

controls.name: AP 1 / AP 2 / A/THR pushbuttons
controls.text: These buttons switch the two autopilots and the autothrust on and off. Autothrust moves the engine power by itself to hold the chosen speed.
controls.context: With the autopilot on, the plane flies itself while the pilots watch.

controls.name: LOC / APPR / EXPED pushbuttons
controls.text: LOC and APPR prepare the autopilot to follow the radio beams of a runway for landing. EXPED makes the plane climb or descend faster.
controls.context: They are pressed when the plane is about to be flown to a landing.

areas.name: Eight display units
areas.text: The big screens in front of the pilots, with the landing gear lever and the autobrake.

panels.name: Display units
panels.text: The A380 has eight big screens. Each pilot has a flying screen and a map screen; the centre has the engine and system screens; the pedestal has two more.
panels.context: The screens can be swapped if one fails, which is why they are called interchangeable.

controls.name: PFD (primary flight display, each pilot)
controls.text: This screen, on the outside edge, shows how the plane flies: tilt, speed, height and the autopilot's mode.
controls.context: It is the main flying screen of each pilot.

controls.name: ND (navigation display, each pilot)
controls.text: This screen shows the map with the plane's route. It has a vertical part showing the plane's path from the side.
controls.context: The EFIS panel sets which map is shown.

controls.name: EWD (engine and warning display)
controls.text: This screen in the upper centre shows engine information and warning messages.
controls.context: The pilots read it after starting the engines and when a warning appears.

controls.name: SD (system display)
controls.text: This screen in the lower centre shows pictures of the plane's systems such as fuel, electricity and air.
controls.context: The ECAM control panel changes the page.

controls.name: MFD (multi-function display, each pilot, on the pedestal)
controls.text: These screens on the pedestal show the pages of the flight computer such as the route and performance. They are used with the keyboard and trackball (KCCU).
controls.context: On the A380 the MFD replaces the small keypad screens that smaller Airbus planes have.

controls.name: Landing gear lever

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The landing gear folds away.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The landing gear is lowered and locked.

controls.text: Moving this lever lifts the wheels after take-off or lowers them before landing.
controls.context: It sits on the centre panel right of the lower screen.

controls.name: Autobrake selector

positions.name: DISARM
positions.text: The automatic braking is off.

positions.name: BTV
positions.text: Brake to vacate: the plane brakes to leave the runway at a chosen exit.

positions.name: LO
positions.text: A gentle automatic braking.
Automatic braking level 2, between gentle and strong.
Automatic braking level 3, stronger than 2.

positions.name: HI
positions.text: The strongest landing autobrake level.

controls.text: This knob chooses how strongly the plane brakes by itself after landing, and arms the brakes for an aborted take-off.
controls.context: The pilot picks the setting before landing.

areas.name: Overhead panel
areas.text: The panels above the pilots with the switches for the plane's systems.

panels.name: Overhead panel
panels.text: These panels over the pilots' heads hold the switches for the plane's systems. Most are lit only if something needs attention.
panels.context: The A380 follows a dark panel idea: a button's light is off in normal condition and comes on if the pilot must act.

controls.name: ADIRS panel
controls.text: This panel turns on the systems that measure where the plane is, which way it points and how fast it flies.
controls.context: The pilots switch these on early because they need time to line up.

controls.name: Flight controls panel (PRIM and SEC)
controls.text: These buttons switch the primary and secondary flight control computers on or off.
controls.context: The computers move the control surfaces according to the stick input, so they are normally left on.

controls.name: Engine / APU fire panel
controls.text: This panel has the fire buttons and extinguisher buttons for each engine and the APU. The APU is a small extra engine in the tail.
controls.context: It is only used if a fire warning comes on.

controls.name: Electrical panel
controls.text: These buttons connect the batteries, the four engine generators and the external ground power to the plane's electric system.
controls.context: The A380 has four engines and so four generators.

controls.name: Fuel panel
controls.text: These buttons control the fuel pumps, the transfer of fuel between tanks and the trim tank, a tank in the tail used to balance the plane.
controls.context: Fuel is moved between tanks to keep the plane balanced.

controls.name: Air and pressurization panels
controls.text: These buttons control the packs, which cool and condition the cabin air, the hot air taken from the engines (bleed air) and the cabin pressure.
controls.context: Pressurization keeps the cabin air comfortable at high altitude.

controls.name: External lights panel
controls.text: These switches turn on the lights outside the plane: strobes, beacon, navigation lights, landing and taxi lights.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to be seen and to see the runway.

areas.name: Pedestal: keyboards, screens and thrust levers
areas.text: The long unit between the pilots with the thrust levers, the keyboards, the radios and the flap and brake handles.

panels.name: Centre pedestal
panels.text: The pedestal is the long unit between the pilots. It holds the thrust levers, the keyboards for the flight computers, the radios and the levers for flaps and speed brakes.
panels.context: The pilots use it on every flight, from engine start to landing.

controls.name: KCCU (keyboard and cursor control unit, each pilot)
controls.text: This is a keyboard with a trackball for each pilot. It is used to type in the route and to move a cursor on the MFD screens.
controls.context: The pilot uses it like a laptop to work the flight computer.

controls.name: Thrust levers 1-4 (IDLE, CL, FLX MCT, TOGA)

positions.name: IDLE
positions.text: The engines run at their lowest power.

positions.name: CL
positions.text: Climb: the normal notch for flying with autothrust.

positions.name: FLX MCT
positions.text: Reduced take-off power or maximum continuous power.

positions.name: TOGA
positions.text: The highest power for take-off or a missed landing.

controls.text: Four levers set the power of the four engines. They click into notches (detents), like on the other Airbus planes.
controls.context: The A380 has four engines, so four levers. The red buttons on them switch autothrust off.

controls.name: Reverser levers (engines 2 and 3)
controls.text: These two levers redirect the thrust of the inner engines forwards to help brake on the ground. They can only be moved when the thrust lever is at IDLE.
controls.context: Only the two inner engines have reversers.

controls.name: Speed brake lever
controls.text: Moving this lever lifts panels on the wings (spoilers) which slow the plane down. Pulling it up arms the ground spoilers for the landing.
controls.context: Armed ground spoilers pop up by themselves after touchdown.

controls.name: Flaps lever

positions.text: Flaps and slats are retracted, for fast flight.
A small step of slats, for take-off and approach.
More flap.
More flap, for approach.

positions.name: FULL
positions.text: The most flap, for landing.

controls.text: This lever extends the flaps and slats, parts of the wing which give more lift at low speed.
controls.context: They are used for take-off and landing.

controls.name: ENG MASTER 1-4 switches

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Fuel is on; the engine starts or keeps running.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Fuel is off; the engine shuts down.

controls.text: Each switch lets fuel flow to one engine and starts it. Turning it OFF stops the engine.
controls.context: They are used for starting the engines and for shutting them down after the flight.

controls.name: ENG MODE selector

positions.name: CRANK
positions.text: Dry or wet motoring: the engine is turned without lighting it.

positions.name: NORM
positions.text: Normal: ignition off, automatic relight.

positions.name: IGN/START
positions.text: The start sequence is armed.

controls.text: This knob between the ENG MASTER switches picks the way the engines turn: motoring, normal, or ready to start.
controls.context: The pilot turns it to IGN/START to begin an engine start.

controls.name: ECAM control panel
controls.text: These buttons choose which system page the lower screen (SD) shows and clear or recall messages.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to look at one system in detail.

controls.name: Radio and audio panels (RMP)
controls.text: These panels set the radio frequencies and choose which radio the pilot talks on.
controls.context: The pilot types the frequency from air traffic control here.

controls.name: PARK BRK handle

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The parking brake is released.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The parking brake is set.

controls.text: This handle sets the parking brake, which holds the wheels still while parked.
controls.context: It is set at the gate and released before moving.

controls.name: RUD TRIM rotary selector and RESET
controls.text: This knob trims the rudder, which gives a small constant push to the tail rudder. Pressing RESET sets the trim back to zero.
controls.context: It is on the trim panel at the back of the pedestal.

controls.name: Pitch trim wheels
controls.text: These wheels on both sides of the thrust levers trim the nose up or down by hand. They are a mechanical trim.
controls.context: Normally the computers trim the plane automatically.

areas.name: Lateral consoles: side-stick, tiller, OIT
areas.text: The consoles at the outer sides of the cockpit, with the side-stick, the steering wheel and the keyboard table.

panels.name: Lateral consoles
panels.text: Each outer side of the cockpit has a console with the side-stick, the steering wheel for taxiing and a table with a keyboard.
panels.context: The captain sits on the left, the first officer on the right; each has their own console.

controls.name: Side-stick
controls.text: A small stick that the pilot moves forward and back to pitch the nose and sideways to roll. It springs back to the centre.
controls.context: The A380 is fly-by-wire: the stick sends orders to the computers which move the control surfaces.

controls.name: Tiller (nosewheel steering)
controls.text: This hand wheel steers the nosewheel and the body gear on the ground, like a car's steering. Pressing it disconnects the pedals from nosewheel steering.
controls.context: The big plane turns slowly on the ground, so the tiller is used for most taxiing.

controls.name: Pull-out table and keyboard (OIT)
controls.text: This pull-out table has a keyboard for the onboard information terminal (OIT), a computer for documents and charts.
controls.context: The pilots use it instead of paper manuals.

controls.name: Oxygen mask
controls.text: A mask which can be put on quickly. It supplies air to breathe if the cabin loses pressure or fills with smoke.
controls.context: Each pilot has one within reach.

areas.name: Side-stick, thrust levers and pedals
areas.text: The things the pilot holds or pushes with the feet.

panels.name: Side-stick buttons and thrust lever grips
panels.text: The buttons on the stick and on the thrust levers that the pilot presses without looking.
panels.context: They give quick access to the radio and to the autopilot and autothrust.

controls.name: Radio communication trigger
controls.text: This trigger on the front of the stick makes the radio transmit while it is held.
controls.context: The pilot talks to air traffic control with it.

controls.name: Takeover / autopilot disconnect pushbutton
controls.text: This red button on the stick switches the autopilot off. Holding it takes priority from the other pilot's stick.
controls.context: It is how a pilot takes the controls.

controls.name: A/THR instinctive disconnect pushbuttons
controls.text: Red buttons on the thrust levers switch autothrust off. Holding for 15 seconds keeps it off for the rest of the flight.
controls.context: The pilot presses it with the thumb to take the power into his own hand.

controls.name: Thrust lever 1
controls.text: This lever sets the power of engine 1, from IDLE up to TOGA.
controls.context: It is the outer left lever of the four.

controls.name: Thrust lever 2
controls.text: This lever sets the power of engine 2, from IDLE up to TOGA.
controls.context: It is the inner left lever; it has a reverser lever.

controls.name: Thrust lever 3
controls.text: This lever sets the power of engine 3, from IDLE up to TOGA.
controls.context: It is the inner right lever; it has a reverser lever.

controls.name: Thrust lever 4
controls.text: This lever sets the power of engine 4, from IDLE up to TOGA.
controls.context: It is the outer right lever of the four.

controls.name: Rudder pedals
controls.text: The pedals move the rudder on the tail to point the nose left or right. The tops of the pedals are the toe brakes for the left and right wheels.
controls.context: They also steer the nosewheel a few degrees.
